prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The map separates a near foreground figure or object at the lower left from a more distant room envelope: the near region is roughly 0.3–1 m from the wearer, while most walls or large surfaces appear about 2–5 m away. Across the five frames, the strongest near region shifts from the far left in frame 1 to the lower centre-right in frames 2–4 and then largely disappears in frame 5, suggesting changing viewpoint, occlusion, or retreat out of view; the overhead bright patches remain above and several metres away. It reveals foreground–background separation that is almost invisible in the dark RGB, but its scale is only approximate and the abrupt brightness changes between frames make metric distance, inter-person distance, and approach versus camera rotation unreliable. Object boundaries also bleed into the background, especially around the lower silhouettes and bright upper-right area, so it cannot reliably establish who faces whom.
descriptions.segmentation: The map detects a partly cropped cat-like foreground shape in frame 2 at the lower centre-left and partly cropped people in frames 3 and 4 at the lower centre-right; no labelled instances appear in frames 1 or 5. These masks locate the detected subjects horizontally and show that their lower portions extend beyond the image boundary, but they provide no direct depth, facing direction, gaze, above/below relationship beyond image coordinates, or reliable arm’s-reach estimate. Combined with the depth map, the masked subjects appear relatively near—roughly 0.5–1.5 m from the wearer—but their distances from one another cannot be recovered because they occur in different time frames rather than simultaneously. The labels are unreliable here: the frame-2 “cat” silhouette resembles the same dark foreground form seen elsewhere, and missed detections in frames 1 and 5 prevent a dependable account of entrances, exits, approach, or retreat.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty in frames 1–4 and shows only a small yellow body configuration near the upper-right of frame 5, with no magenta hand skeletons anywhere. In frame 5 the detected person is several metres ahead and to the wearer’s right, appears tilted or nearly horizontal in the image, and is not within the wearer’s arm’s reach; the sparse joints do not reliably determine facing direction, gaze toward the wearer, or exact limb placement. No second pose is present, so distances between people, mutual orientation, and what lies within another person’s reach cannot be established, while parts of the detected body may be missing or merged. The map exposes a possible human configuration that is nearly invisible in the RGB, but the absence of poses in the first four frames and the fragmented frame-5 skeleton make temporal claims about turning, approach, retreat, and occlusion unreliable.
